overall: The AG found the committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the email exchange about scheduling was not deliberation, and the AG declined to review whether a non-chair member could post notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a quorum of the committee deliberated outside a posted meeting through email exchanges about scheduling a reorganization meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Although a close question, we find that the emails that are the subject of the complaints here focused on scheduling a meeting, and therefore did not constitute deliberation outside a meeting in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 14 meeting was illegal because its notice was posted by a member other than the chair.
allegations.key_passage: Because the posting of notice of a meeting by a member other than the chair, even if true, would not be a violation of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review this allegation.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
